summary.headline: DOMS Q2 FY27 revenue rose 17.6% to INR667.8 crore, but EBITDA margin held at 12.4% as raw material inflation (~15%) outpaced pricing.
summary.overview: Operating revenue grew 17.6% YoY to INR667.8 crore in Q2 FY27 and 18.4% in H1, with over 80% of growth from volume. EBITDA was INR82.8 crore in Q2 and INR165.3 crore in H1, both at a 12.4% margin, with the quarter held sequentially flat despite a sharp raw material rebound from August. Flooding in Gujarat cut sales growth by an estimated 300-350 bps and caused a one-time INR10.4 crore exceptional loss, for which insurance claims have been filed. Management chose a patient, measured pricing stance, deferring a more aggressive margin-recovery push by a couple of quarters, and guided consolidated sales growth of 18-20% for the year.

financial_highlights.change: margin 5.7%; includes INR10.4 crore one-time flood exceptional loss
EBITDA margin 6.4% vs 8.1% a year ago

segments.name: Scholastic stationery, art and office supplies
segments.commentary: Broad-based growth on capacity added over the last year; office supplies and adhesives named as main growth drivers. Kits and combos grew only marginally due to capacity constraints.

segments.name: Hobby and craft (adhesives)
segments.commentary: Strong momentum from an expanded adhesive range and added capacity; management expects it to be a key growth driver.

segments.name: Back-to-school
segments.commentary: Strong growth led by the recently launched pencil box range; compass and school box range is early but gaining traction.

segments.name: Hygiene / Uniclan (baby diapers, wet wipes)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 21.5% with both volume and price; EBITDA margin fell to 6.4% from 8.1% on raw material costs. Long-term target 8-10%.

segments.name: Reynolds writing instruments
segments.commentary: Production started in the first 50-acre building (~170,000 sq ft) for Brite and 045, with Jetter click pen in trial. Revenue expected from Q3 FY27, gaining momentum in Q4; MRP kept unchanged.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated sales growth guided at 18-20% for FY27, reiterated despite the flood impact.

Long-term EBITDA margin target of 16-17%; management says it will be patient for a couple of quarters before deciding on significant pricing action. Pre-West Asia conflict consolidated margin was close to 17%.
Capex of INR100-125 crore expected in H2 FY27 after over INR200 crore in H1.
Debt of about INR100-120 crore needed in the midterm to fund capex; internal accruals expected to fund more once margins normalise.

Reynolds business plan expected to be clearer by next quarter; management said a one-year timeline for reaching the INR150 crore pre-acquisition writing instrument revenue would be cut to nine months.
Detailed FY28 outlook deferred to January-February discussion.
capex_capacity: First building of 50-acre greenfield facility commissioned (~170,000 sq ft) for office supplies and Reynolds pens; second and third buildings have machinery being installed; three more buildings at finishing stage.
Planned additions in the new facility: wooden pencil manufacturing and further office supplies capacity before FY27 close; pen tip manufacturing being installed for backward integration.
H1 FY27 capex over INR200 crore, mainly for the 50-acre site, land adjacent (footprint raised from 45 to 50 acres), machinery and Reynolds asset purchase.
Uniclan added one baby diaper line and one wet wipes line; spare capacity remains, so no further capex planned until FY28-29 review.
Seven SpA JV: DOMS Seven Private Limited incorporated in October as a wholly owned vehicle; Seven SpA to take 50% stake once documents (apostille) and JV agreement are finalised.
demand_pricing: Volume contributed over 80% of the ~18% revenue growth; realisation about 20%.
Raw material inflation was about 15% after early-quarter cooling; price increases were taken selectively at SKU level, with schemes and discounts reduced versus last year.
Price increases took 3-4 months to reach the market because of MRP-based pricing and about two months of printed packing inventory.
Raw material prices rose from early-to-mid August and kept increasing through October, with price changes happening once or twice a week.
Net consumption impact is about 9% of costs, versus about 10% in Q1.
Regional: West slowed due to lower merchant exports to Bangladesh after geopolitical disruption; management says consumption is evenly spread across four regions.
Reynolds fixed overheads (team integration) cost about 0.5-1% of sales in Q2, a temporary margin drag.

qa_highlights.question: Split of growth between volume and realisation, and how much raw material inflation has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: More than 80% of the ~18% growth was volume and about 20% realisation. Pricing is calibrated and lags the market, with management describing it as a catch-up game.

qa_highlights.question: What is the realistic margin outlook and why not pass through faster?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged near-term margin pressure. The 16-17% target stands, but it will wait a couple of quarters before deciding on more significant action, and says this is not a commitment to a specific quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is Reynolds integrated, and why relocate its manufacturing?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales and support teams are fully integrated under the field force, with some distributor rightsizing. Moulds and assembly machines were moved from Chennai to Umbergaon because the Chennai infrastructure was not part of the deal. Pricing is unchanged for now.

qa_highlights.question: Why not start the new plant with pencils, given less raw material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Pens were always the priority given market opportunity. Machine lead times of six to eight months were ordered before the conflict. Management says the timing difference is about one quarter at most.

qa_highlights.question: How much debt is being added and what is the peak?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt has roughly doubled from March to about INR200 crore, funding capex, Reynolds and working capital. Management expects it to need INR100-120 crore more in the midterm.

qa_highlights.question: How long does the industry take to pass through inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: At DOMS, full capture of an inflation cycle has taken about 18-24 months from the start, and the company has already spent two quarters in it.

qa_highlights.question: Is the raw material basket up 15% versus 10% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Inflation is about 15%. The 10% figure in Q1 was the impact on consumption, now about 9%, an improvement of about 2 points.

risks_watch: Raw material costs still rising into October and linked to West Asia conflict and crude; no margin visibility guided.
Margin recovery to 16-17% depends on pricing actions that are deferred by a couple of quarters; a further squeeze is possible if costs keep rising.
Reynolds ramp-up: revenue expected only from Q3 FY27, and the margin drag from integrated staff costs needs to normalise.
Rising debt and working capital needs (about INR100-120 crore more in the midterm) while free cash flow is weaker.
Flood-related disruption and the INR10.4 crore loss; insurance recovery timing is not fixed.
Bangladesh export disruption affecting West region sales.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume and capacity, but cautious and evasive on margins: management repeatedly said visibility is limited and chose to be patient rather than commit to a margin recovery timeline. Deferred FY28 and detailed Reynolds questions to later calls.
key_quotes: So it's like a catch-up game that we are playing, and we will take calibrated actions wherever we believe that there is possibility to increase the prices.
We follow a very simple mantra nothing at the cost of market and at the same time, nothing at the cost of margin.
But what we've seen at DOMS is about 18 to 24 months. That is the outer limit from the start of the cycle.
